title: Tiny Onramp Scenarios and SAGE Checklist (draft)
body:
Purpose
------
This is a lightweight working doc for a tiny, low-friction onramp experience we can ship to get new engineers and integrators to a useful demo within 20 minutes. The idea: a minimal CLI + in-browser playground + local stub that exercise the core happy path and a couple of realistic failure/fallback flows (SAGE: Simple, Actionable, Guided, Explanatory).

Goals
-----
- 20-minute end-to-end: sign up -> API key -> run a sample CLI request -> open playground and stream response.
- Demonstrate: generation, streaming, function/tool calling, and embeddings (mini example).
- Provide clear safety net: automatic fallback to local stub or smaller model when rate-limited or in local mode.
- Minimal telemetry contract for the first hour to measure adoption: sdk.init, sdk.call, sdk.fallback, sdk.error, playground-run.

Audience and constraints
------------------------
Primary: product/feature engineers and platform teams who want to evaluate latency, cost, and integration complexity. Constraints: should work with only Node/Python installed (no container runtime required), small footprint (no GPU), and not require corporate VPN.

User flows (SAGE-focused)
------------------------
1) CLI quickstart (15–20 min)
   - prereqs: Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, curl optional.
   - steps: npm init redwood-llm; set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; redwood demo chat --model lite-1 --prompt "Summarize our README"
   - expected output: streaming tokens printed to the terminal, final summary, cost estimate printed at end.
   - failure modes handled: no API key -> interactive helper that opens the dashboard signup link; request throttled -> message explaining rate limit with explicit TTL and automatic backoff attempt (3 tries) then offer local stub.

2) Playground quickloop (10–15 min)
   - embedded in web UI (static html + tiny JS) or served locally via `redwood play`.
   - shows streaming, response options (raw, json schema validation), and a function-call example: call a mock calendar API with structured JSON result.
   - SAGE: guided prompt presets, explanation tooltips on cost/latency for each preset.

3) Local stub and dev-mode (for offline/demo)
   - `redwood dev-proxy --local-stub` provides an HTTP proxy that returns canned responses and emulates streaming.
   - Use case: demos without a network or for workshops. Telemetry switches to opt-out mode for privacy in local stub.

Minimal SDK surface we will show in docs
---------------------------------------
- Initialize: Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY})
- chat.stream({model, messages}) -> readable stream
- embeddings.create({model, input}) -> array of vectors
- tools.register('calendar', schema, handler) + model.requestTool('calendar', args)

Telemetry contract (MVP)
-----------------------
Events (name, minimal payload)
- sdk.init: {sdk_language, sdk_version, has_api_key (bool)}
- sdk.call: {endpoint, model, tokens_estimate, latency_ms}
- sdk.fallback: {reason: "rate_limit"|"model_unavailable"|"local_mode", fallback: "local_stub"|"lite-1"}
- sdk.error: {code, message}
- playground.run: {preset, duration_ms}
Notes: no user-identifying data. Send hashed project id if available. Provide a single opt-out env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0.

Docs/UX copy snippets (for the quickstart page)
------------------------------------------------
- Headline: "Run Redwood in under 20 minutes — CLI + Playground"
- Subhead: "Try generation, streaming, and tools without a heavy setup."
- CTA button: "Get API key (free tier)" -> links to hosted signup.
- Error copy example for throttling: "We hit a short-term rate limit. We'll retry for you. If the problem persists, switch to local demo mode with --local-stub."

Edge/failure scenarios to show explicitly
----------------------------------------
- Rate limit: automatic retry, then fallback to local stub.
- Partial streaming break (network drop): resume suggestion + last-good-tokens shown.
- Schema validation failure for tool call: pretty diff + developer link to schema guide.
- No API key: interactive flow that points to dashboard and creates a one-click sample key for demos (internal-only flag).

Files to include in the tiny package
----------------------------------
- README.md (clear 3-step run)
- cli/ (mini CLI script)
- playground/ (single static page + small server)
- local-stub/ (express/fastapi minimal service)
- examples/ (chat.js, embeddings.py, tool_call_example.js)
- telemetry.md (what events we send + opt-out)

Acceptance criteria for a launchable MVP (team-level)
-----------------------------------------------------
- 1-click bootstrap (npm init or pip install) + demo chat runs locally.
- Playground returns a streaming response in <1s median on hosted infra for the demo model.
- Telemetry emits the 5 events and can be toggled off.
- Docs: quickstart page + troubleshooting section + CLI reference.
- Internal playbook for the first-week support: triage checklist and common fixes (faq).

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Which demo model should be the default? Options: lite-1 (low-cost) vs conversational-1 (higher quality). Need perf/cost matrix. (Action: Rafael to run a micro-benchmark by 2025-11-10)
- Should we auto-create ephemeral demo API keys for anonymous sessions? Security review needed. (Action: Priya to scope and raise JIRA-SEC-232)
- Telemetry: how long do we retain event sampling? baseline: 30 days. Confirm with privacy. (Action: Ethan to sync with security)
- Local stub content: should include 3 canned personas (support, marketing, engineering). Who authors copy? (Action: Ava to draft)

Notes to self / informal
-----------------------
- Keep the code examples intentionally tiny (<30 LOC) — the mental overhead is the killer.
- Playground should emphasize streaming visually (growing bubble) — that 'wow' moment helps adoption.
- If we ship a single repo, provide a `template/` directory for teams to fork for internal hacks.

Quick timeline proposal (2-week sprint slice)
-------------------------------------------
Week 1: prototype CLI + local-stub + README + basic telemetry emitters.
Week 2: playground, scaffolding for ephemeral keys (if approved), docs, and internal playtest.

Slack snippets / links (for copy-paste during demos)
--------------------------------------------------
- "Run: npm i -g redwood-mini && REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> redwood demo chat --prompt \"Summarize README\""
- Internal test invite: https://redwood-internal/teams/devx/onramp-playtest

Appendix: sample terminal session (condensed)
-------------------------------------------
$ export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxx
$ redwood demo chat --prompt "Top 3 takeaways from our README"
> streaming: "1) Lightweight SDKs..."
> streaming: "2) Production-first…"
> final: "Summary (tokens: 86, estimated cost: $0.004)"

End of draft.

(If this looks good I will spin up a tiny repo and assign initial PRs: CLI, playground, local-stub, docs.)
